title: AI thumbnails get fewer clicks. Show buyers the real thing.
summary: Your show thumbnail is your first chance to show shoppers what you’re selling. Your inventory, taste, and expertise give people a reason to shop with you. A generic AI-style image can hide those strengths before a buyer ever enters your show.
body_markdown:
You can now make an image of almost anything in seconds. A dragon guarding a mountain of trading cards. A cartoon version of yourself surrounded by sneakers. An image packed with slogans or flashing sale signs.


But if you’re selling a great pair of jeans, buyers want to see the jeans.


This Black Friday lead with what you’re selling. Your inventory, taste, and expertise give people a reason to shop with you. A generic AI-style image can hide those strengths before a buyer ever enters your show.


And there’s an engaged audience ready to shop with you this holiday season. More than one in four Americans say shopping from home through a live show is more appealing than visiting stores during the holidays*. Your show thumbnail is your first chance to show shoppers what you’re selling.


### **We studied 2.4 million shows. Real inventory stood out.**


Buyers have seen more than 38 billion show thumbnail impressions on Whatnot this year. Before they hear a seller explain a watch’s history or meet the collectors in the chat, they see an image. We wanted to understand what makes them take that next step.


We studied 2.4 million shows from nearly 200,000 US sellers, focusing on people discovering sellers they didn’t already follow. We compared shows from the same seller in the same category, accounting for factors including feed position, timing, and show format.


A wall of real inventory was associated with 4.8% more taps from new viewers. Images with more than 20 words of text saw 5.6% fewer. And the pattern was even stronger for smaller sellers. Shows with real-inventory thumbnails saw about 13% more taps from new viewers, while thumbnails with more than 20 words of text had about 8% fewer.


Those taps turned into sales: inventory-wall shows saw roughly 3-6% more sales from new shoppers over the next 30 days, and text-heavy images roughly 6-9% *less* . A stocked shelf, rack of clothing, or table filled with cards may seem ordinary when you work beside it every day. To someone looking for a gift they won’t find anywhere else, it could be the most interesting thing in their feed.


### **Give new buyers a reason to join your show**


First impressions matter, especially in live commerce, where your thumbnail can determine whether a new buyer ever enters your show.


Before your Black Friday show, look at yours through a new buyer’s eyes:


-


**Show what’s actually for sale.** Feature the vintage rack, stocked shelves, or card selection buyers can expect to find in your show.


-


**Keep text short and useful.** Give buyers room to see the merchandise. Our study found that images with more than 20 words were associated with fewer taps.


-


**Check your AI images.** Can a shopper tell what you sell, or could the image belong to almost any business? If the products are lost, swap it for a real inventory photo.


Then deliver on that first impression. Around 30% of Gen Z and Millennial adults said real-time seller interaction would make them more likely to buy holiday gifts live*. Once buyers join, put your expertise on display: explain what makes an item special, answer questions, and help them find what they’re looking for.


### **Put AI to work for your business**


AI images aren’t drawing buyers in, which raises a useful question: what should we ask AI to do?


AI should help sellers build their businesses and help buyers find things they want. That might mean reducing administrative work or connecting a shopper with a seller whose inventory matches their interests.


Generating a promotional image should face the same test: does it help a customer understand what’s for sale? For Whatnot, that means using findings like these to shape the product. We’re working toward bringing thumbnail guidance into show creation, where it can help sellers as they choose an image.


You’ve put the work into sourcing inventory and planning a show worth visiting. This Black Friday, give shoppers a clear look at what you’ve found. Read more in our[Help Center](https://help.whatnot.com/hc/en-us/articles/50093385413773-Thumbnail-Best-Practices) .


Happy selling!


– Whatnot Product Team


**Data Source: Public First omnibus survey, October 20-23, 2026, n=2006, US adults 18+.*
